blocks.body: File last year's return by the April deadline. Until that deadline, not counting extensions, you can still make an IRA or HSA contribution for last year. Then run the IRS Tax Withholding Estimator with a current pay stub and file a new W-4 if the projection is far from zero — especially after a raise, a second job, a marriage or a new child. If you pay estimated tax, put the four due dates on the calendar: April 15, June 15, September 15 and January 15.

If you pay estimated tax, mark the four due dates on your calendar: April 15, June 15, September 15 and January 15.

blocks.body: Before December 31: harvest tax losses in taxable accounts if useful, but do not buy a substantially identical holding within 30 days before or after in any account, including an IRA or a spouse's, or the loss will not count. Ask the custodian early for any required minimum distribution (including one from an inherited IRA), qualified charitable distribution or Roth conversion, so it is done by December 31. A first RMD can wait until April 1 of the next year, but then two are due that year. Use up any health FSA money that would be lost when its plan year ends, make planned charitable gifts, and use the gift annual exclusion ({{fig:gift_annual_exclusion}} per recipient for 2026) if gifting.
blocks.plain: Before December 31: sell investments at a loss in taxable accounts if it helps. But don't buy the same or a nearly identical investment within 30 days before or after, in any account, including an IRA or your spouse's, or the loss won't count. Ask your account company early for any required minimum distribution (including one from an inherited IRA), qualified charitable distribution or Roth conversion, so it is done by December 31. Your first required minimum distribution can wait until April 1 of the next year, but then you must take two that year. Use up health FSA money you would otherwise lose when the plan year ends. Make planned gifts to charity, and use the yearly gift exclusion ({{fig:gift_annual_exclusion}} per person for 2026) if you're giving to anyone.
